Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov_ph s. 2621 OPINION NO. AUG 21 n MR. RUBEN B. TAMAYO Naguilian Sur, Ilagan City, Isabela rubenbtamay031@gmail.com Dear Mr. Tamayo. This has reference to your letter dated 15 April 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion on the following: I. What is the basis in determining the location of certain structure or property? 2. Who has the authority to decide the location of a business establishment? Per the representation, there is an ongoing construction of a medical school in barangay Naguilian Sur, Iligan City. You then represented that your brother, who happens to be the punong barangay of Naguilian Sur, told you that the medical school will be under the barangay Lullutan as it was already announced by the City Mayor's Office. You stated that you believe that the medical school should be under the jurisdiction of Naguilian Sur. Thus, the request for legal opinion. In your first query, the basis in determining the location of certain structure or property depends on various factors, which can include the following: I. 2. 3. 4. 5. Accessibility: The accessibility of people and vehicles to the location. Proximity to roads, highways, public transportation, etc., is crucial. Zoning Regulations: Local government regulations and ordinances dictate where certain types of structures can be built (residential, commercial, industrial, etc.) as provided by Section 2151 of the Local Government Code of 1991. Environmental Factors: Considerations like flood zones, soil stability, presence of wetlands, and ecological impact assessments through the office of the City Environment and National Resources Office (CENRO) play a role. Legal and Regulatory Requirements: Compliance with building codes and the Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLUP) of the Municipality. Economic Considerations: Cost of land, construction, maintenance, and potential resale value are economic factors. 1 Section 215. Classes of Real Property for Assessment Purposes. - For purposes of assessment, real property shall be classified as residential, agricultural, commercial, industrial, mineral, timberland or special. The city or municipality within the Metropolitan Manila Area, through their respective sanggunian, shall have the power to classify lands as residential, agricultural. commercial, industrial, mineral, timberland, or special in accordance with their zoning ordinances. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Determining the optimal location involves balancing these factors to ensure that the chosen site meets the needs and objectives of the project or property development. As to the second quer_y, in LGUs, the local zoning board or planning department has the authority to determine the location of a business establishment through zoning ordinances which are designed to promote orderly development, protect property values, and ensure compatibility of land uses. As to the duties of local zoning board, said office reviews proposals for new business establishments to ensure they comply with local zoning regulations. In the matter at hand, considering that the medical school is a business establishment, it should follow the City's regulations and ordinances. It is the City, through the local zoning board, that has the authority to determine whether the business establishment has met the conditions of local zoning ordinances for new business establishments. Thus, the medical school being constructed should be under the supervision of the City of Ilagan rather than Barangay Lullutan or Barangay Naguilian Sur. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, HORITY OF THE SECRETARY: N 'TOR R. LLAMAS nde cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OU LLA/JVRULLLS-LRALLD/lasm Page 2 of 2
